questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: (i) Experiences from friends and co-workers, (ii) availability of relevant course, taught in English, (iii) relative proximity to home, (iv) specific connection with the language of the host university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Practical information regarding class rooms, introduction module etc. was easily accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None personally.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Personally had no difficulties - out of mere luck rather than preparation - but other students faced difficulties applying for and changing courses, despite these changes being necessitated because of changes in the course descriptions which lead to courses not being pre-approved.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy through agencies; just expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The staff at ESADE themselves adviced against living in certain areas of the city, but this was not communicated publicly to the students before the semester began. Either research thoroughly or settle with living in areas with relatively high crime rates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Descriptions (and even names) of the courses were published very late (June/July) and often changed afterwards. This made it very difficult to coordinate with our home university in terms of ensuring pre-approval of the courses; often pre-approvals were not finished before the semester started. In essence, there was no way for us to complete the steps required for our Erasmus grant until several months into the exchange.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Students make a prioritized list of 10 subjects (all between 3-6 ECTS) in a web-page which only allows for certain overlaps. After the selection period is over, students are automatically assigned between 27 and 33 ECTS points worth of courses - no matter the requirement of the sending university(!) The system regularly assigned courses not on the prioritized list and even assigned business courses to law students... Students were made to attempt to rectify these errors themselves during a change period, but because all classes were technically "full", changes could usually not be made by students. In the end, every student with wrong courses (a large portion of the students) had to book a physical meeting with the EASDE exchange program manager to have their courses fixed. Overall a bad process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: See the answer above.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Relatively successful. After recieving 5 courses from my prioritized list and 2 courses not on my prioritized list (one of which being a business course in geoeconomics), I only had to exchange one course in order to reach 30 ECTS worth of law courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare to get annoyed; you'll probably have to figure it all out after you have already arrived and hope for the best.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academic program was varied and included many interesting subjects.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were relatively easy. Simply showing up for the weekly 2 hour lecture and paying attention was adequate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was no pre-defined curriculum. Rather, the students just had to pay attention in class, read the professor's PowerPoint slides and a handful of articles.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: (i) Comparative Law, (ii) Diplomatic & Consular Law and Practice, (iii) Financial Systems: Banking, Markets & Insurance, (iv) International Criminal and Humanitarian Law, (v) International Sales Law, (vi) Legal Aspects of Real Estate Transactions, and (vii) World Trade Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally, I would recommend all of the above except Comparative Law. The professors were committed, and the course material was relevant to law students.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As far as I know, only sports were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any non-academic activities at the host institution, so I do not know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the sights and museums of the city, go to the beach with other students, go on Erasmus trips (to the surrounding mountains, to Andorra, to Morocco etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very. It is very similar, only regular meal times etc. are shifted.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A general sense of being relaxed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: (i) Prepare to be annoyed by the course selection, (ii) knowing a bit of Spanish goes a long way, and (iii) research online before choosing a place a live.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being the intermediary between the sending university and the host university regarding pre-approvals necessary for the Erasmus grant.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
